s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive spinal cord syndrome with acute worsening of motor weakness
salient_findings: Gradually progressive motor weakness of the left lower extremity
Superficial hypoesthesia below the T7 level
key_facts: 68-year-old retired man
No prior medical history
Two months of dorsal spine pain
Gradually progressive motor weakness of the left lower extremity
Acute worsening of weakness one week before admission
Unable to stand or walk without assistance
No history of trauma
Spastic paraparesis with weakness of the quadriceps, hamstrings, ankle dorsiflexors, and toe extensors on the left
Increased patellar and ankle jerks
Sustained clonus at the left ankle
Bilateral Babinski signs
Superficial hypoesthesia present below the T7 level
Bladder and bowel function preserved
Extra-axial mass posterolateral to the right side of the spinal cord at C7–T1
Marked canal stenosis and cord deformation

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Extra-axial mass with dural tail and marked canal stenosis

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass with intermediate signal intensity on T1-weighted images

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive motor weakness and extra-axial mass

shortlist.label: Hemangiopericytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Extra-axial mass with thin rim of enhancement

shortlist.label: Spinal cord metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute worsening of motor weakness and extra-axial mass

raw.rationale: The lesion is described as a well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass with a thin rim of enhancement and no internal enhancement on MRI, which is consistent with the typical appearance of a meningioma. Additionally, the location posterolateral to the spinal cord and the presence of marked canal stenosis and cord deformation are also consistent with a meningioma.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are typically more heterogeneous in signal intensity and may have a more variable pattern of enhancement.

rejected.label: Neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibromas are often associated with neurofibromatosis type 1 and may have a more complex appearance on MRI.

rejected.label: Hemangiopericytoma
rejected.why: Hemangiopericytomas are rare and typically have a more aggressive appearance on MRI, with heterogeneous signal intensity and irregular enhancement.

rejected.label: Spinal cord metastasis
rejected.why: Metastases to the spinal cord are typically multiple and may have a more irregular appearance on MRI, with heterogeneous signal intensity and enhancement.
